q: The concept of temperature is very important for the physical and biological sciences.
e: True. The concept of temperature is very important for the physical and biological sciences. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The temperature of an object is directly related to the energies of molecules composing the object.
e: True. The temperature of an object is directly related to the energies of molecules composing the object. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Natural processes often involve energy changes and the temperature is an indicator for these changes.
e: True. Natural processes often involve energy changes and the temperature is an indicator for these changes. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Thermal energy is an internal energy of a matter.
e: True. Thermal energy is an internal energy of a matter. Thermal energy is an internal energy of a matter is anything that has mass and occupies space.

q: Heat is considered to be a form of energy.
e: True. Heat is considered to be a form of energy. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: Heat and temperature are the same quantities.
e: False. Heat is transferred energy. Temperature is the hotness scale. They are not the same quantity.

q: Temperature is the quantity that determines how cold (or) how hot the object is.
e: True. Temperature is the quantity that determines how cold (or) how hot the object is. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The temperature of a hot body is lower than that of a cold body.
e: False. A hot body has a higher temperature than a cold body. That is what hot means. Temperature tells you the hotness.

q: To measure temperature accurately, we use instruments called thermometers.
e: True. To measure temperature accurately, we use instruments called thermometers. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The energy exchanged between an object and its surrounding due to different temperatures is defined as heat.
e: True. The energy exchanged between an object and its surrounding due to different temperatures is defined as heat. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: Heat is the energy in transit.
e: True. Heat is the energy in transit. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: The unit of heat is different from the units of energy.
e: False. Heat is energy, so it uses the joule, the same SI energy unit. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: When a body at a higher temperature is in contact with a body at a lower temperature, heat flows from the second to the first body.
e: False. Heat flows from the hotter body to the colder body, never the reverse by itself. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: The motions and positions of molecules in matter result in the kinetic energy and potential energy.
e: True. The motions and positions of molecules in matter result in the kinetic energy and potential energy. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

q: The total energy, that is, the sum of the potential energy and the kinetic energy, of molecules in matter is in fact the external energy of that matter.
e: False. Molecular kinetic plus potential energy is internal energy, not external energy. Raise a mass or stretch a spring and you store potential energy.

q: Temperature is a measure of the internal energy of molecules.
e: True. Temperature is a measure of the internal energy of molecules. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.
